dynamics.title: A French flagship, a German headquarters and a new leadership culture at the top

items.text: SeLoger has had a German parent since 2011 (Axel Springer) and a Berlin-headquartered group, AVIV, since 2021. French staff have long linked German ownership with restructuring: in 2018 Logic-Immo employees petitioned against the SeLoger takeover, citing the social cost they expected from "the German group's model".

Since March 2025 AVIV is led by a CEO who spent a decade scaling Avito, Russia's largest classifieds business, and moved it from advertising to transactions. His predecessor came from Expedia. Together with KKR's ownership, this points to a faster, more monetisation-focused and more top-down rhythm from the group. The rhythm is an inference; the careers are documented.

On the map, French and Russian business cultures sit close together on hierarchy, top-down decisions, relationship-based trust and high-context communication. Berlin's group functions are the outlier: explicit, consensus-first, schedule-driven. In practice, Paris may adapt to the group's top more easily than to its processes, and Berlin functions may find both Paris and the group leadership hard to plan around.
2021–25 centralised product on one European platform; 2026 swung back to French autonomy. Both moves cost French jobs, so every shift in the balance between Paris and the group is felt personally.

France is AVIV's flagship consumer platform, yet the CEO, the pricing architecture, group functions and owner governance sit outside France. Paris has the scale; the group and the owners hold the frameworks.

Group roles, including Paris roles, are advertised in English; agents, federations and unions work in French. Expect French as the operating language and English for anything involving the group or investors.

dynamics.note: Search-partner input reports that more senior roles have gone to people from Russian business backgrounds. Public sources confirm the CEO's career but name no other such hires, so the scale of this shift needs client validation.

culture.dimensionsTitle: What the eight dimensions look like at SeLoger and AVIV

dimensions.tension: Group top and Paris vs Berlin functions

views.fr: The senior leader decides after open debate; decisions can be reopened with new arguments.
views.de: Agreement is built first, often slowly; once agreed, the decision is fixed.
views.ru: The most senior person decides, quickly; the decision is communicated as final.

dimensions.scene: The group leadership sets France's 2027 pricing direction after a short discussion and treats it as settled. Paris wants to debate the reasoning; the Berlin pricing function had planned a longer alignment process and has not finished its analysis. Each side sees the others as the problem.
dimensions.helps: Clarify which decisions are taken at the top and which are delegated. Explain the why to Paris; give Berlin functions a defined window; once decided, reopen only with new facts.

dimensions.tension: Group top vs Berlin; Paris in between

views.fr: Hierarchical: titles and the director's role carry weight.
views.de: Moderate: structure matters, but people engage directly across levels.
views.ru: Strongly hierarchical: authority is concentrated at the top and expected to be visible.

dimensions.scene: A group executive asks a Paris team lead directly for figures, bypassing the French director. Paris reads it as undermining; Berlin colleagues see nothing unusual; the group executive expects the answer the same day.
dimensions.helps: Agree channels between group and France explicitly. As a France leader, protect your managers' authority while answering the group fast.

dimensions.tension: Berlin functions vs Paris and group top

views.fr: Meaning partly carried by context and nuance; actions not always written down.
views.de: Explicit, precise, written; what is said is what is meant.
views.ru: High-context: priorities and displeasure are often signalled rather than spelled out.

dimensions.scene: In a quarterly review the group leadership says « let's see how the regions perform ». Paris reads a warning about the regional budget; Berlin waits for a written instruction that never comes.
dimensions.helps: After every group meeting, write down decisions, owners and dates and confirm them. Ask directly what a signal means for your budget or plan.

dimensions.tension: Berlin functions vs group top and Paris

views.de: Linear: agendas, sequences and deadlines are firm.
views.ru: Flexible: plans change quickly with circumstances and leadership priorities.

dimensions.scene: The group changes a France priority between two planning cycles. Berlin's planning calendar breaks; Paris adapts but late; the PE reporting date does not move.
dimensions.helps: Separate fixed dates (investor reporting, legal consultation steps) from movable ones, and flag slippage early.

dimensions.tension: Berlin functions vs group top and Paris

views.fr: Trust grows through relationships and time together.
views.ru: Strongly relationship-based: personal trust with senior leaders speeds everything up.

dimensions.scene: Leaders with a direct relationship to the group CEO get faster decisions; others experience slower approvals and see an inner circle. A new hire who only delivers documents on time is respected in Berlin but not yet trusted at the top.
dimensions.helps: Invest early in personal relationships with the group leadership and with Paris teams, and earn Berlin's trust by delivering exactly what was promised.

views.fr: Fairly direct criticism, usually framed by reasoned argument.
views.ru: Very direct negative feedback, often blunt, sometimes in front of others.

dimensions.scene: A group business review criticises France's lead numbers bluntly in front of the French team. Paris accepts directness but feels the missing reasoning and the public setting as a loss of face.
dimensions.helps: Receive blunt feedback without taking it personally; when passing it on to Paris teams, add the reasoning and deliver sensitive points one to one.

views.fr: Open debate is expected and not personal.
views.ru: Disagreement is accepted, though openly challenging the most senior person is rarer.

dimensions.scene: Paris debates freely in its own comité de direction but goes quieter in front of the group CEO. Newcomers from more confrontation-avoiding backgrounds may lose influence in Paris debates.
dimensions.helps: Debate openly in Paris; with the group top, challenge with data, in the right setting, before the decision is final.

views.ru: Principles-first leaning, but at group level PE pressure favours results-first messages.

dimensions.scene: A France leader presents a full conceptual case to the group and is asked for the number and the decision first; the same deck without the reasoning would fail in Paris.
dimensions.helps: Prepare two versions: results-first for the group and investors, reasoning-first for Paris.

joining.eyebrow: For an executive joining from outside France
joining.title: What to expect in the first six months

items.title: Decisions may come fast and from the top.
items.text: The group's leadership and owners favour speed. Expect priorities to be set or changed at group level with short notice and to be treated as final; your job is to execute and explain them, then raise concerns with data.

items.title: Reasoning before conclusions in Paris.
items.text: French teams expect the logic behind a decision and will challenge it in debate. That is engagement, not resistance.

items.title: Hierarchy and channels matter.
items.text: In Paris and at the group top, titles and reporting lines carry weight. Going around a director, or letting group colleagues do so, undermines them.

items.title: Relationships unlock delivery.
items.text: Trust is built personally, in Paris and with the group leadership. Skipping that to be efficient reads as distance.

items.title: Change goes through employee representatives.
items.text: Reorganisations require consultation of the works council (CSE) on legal timelines; the 2026 plan needed union agreement. The group's pace and France's process have to be reconciled by you.

items.title: You may be seen as "the group's person".
items.text: After two restructurings, an outside hire can be read as an extension of Berlin, the group leadership or the funds. Local legitimacy has to be earned.

items.title: French is the working language with customers and teams.
items.text: Whether professional French is required depends on the role; confirm it with the client.

hiring.title: Assess adaptability, never nationality

items.title: Test for working under a fast, top-down leadership.
items.text: Ask how the candidate executed decisions taken quickly above them, and how they pushed back with evidence without slowing delivery.

items.title: Test the Berlin gap.
items.text: Deciding, scheduling and communicating create most friction with group functions. Ask how they worked with a slower, more process-driven head office.

items.title: Look for evidence of bridging.
items.text: Leaders of a country unit inside a foreign-headquartered group, or people who sat between a head office and a local team, and can show how they adapted each way.

items.title: Value experience with negotiated change.
items.text: Leading through works councils or unions transfers well; pure "announce and execute" experience transfers badly in France.

items.title: Make language explicit.
items.text: State the French and English requirement per role up front.

items.title: Reference in three directions.
items.text: Ask a former boss, a peer at head office and a member of the local team how the candidate was perceived.

hiring.note: Nationality, origin or cultural similarity, including similarity to the group's leadership, are never selection criteria. The aim is to assess a capability: reading and adapting to these working styles.

businessInsights.title: The market SeLoger is fighting in

cards.title: Agent trust is the main commercial vulnerability
cards.text: Agents pay the bills, and many still resent the 2023 private-listing opening and price rises. Their federations co-own a rival and are campaigning on pricing again in 2026. Every pricing or product rule is read politically.

cards.title: The Paris core is under attack
cards.text: Leboncoin, historically strongest in the provinces, is now targeting Île-de-France, the most valuable market and SeLoger's stronghold, with new packages and marketing.

cards.title: An agent-owned challenger with a loyalty edge
cards.text: Bien'ici sells itself as professional-only and agent-controlled, grew visits 14% in 2025 and wants first place. It competes on the relationship SeLoger is trying to repair.

cards.title: A new entrant with a proven playbook
cards.text: idealista enters France in 2026 under a former Leboncoin real-estate head. Its impact is unknown, but it adds a fourth front.

cards.title: Growth through regions and acquisitions
cards.text: Regional sales teams, a Grand Ouest acquisition giving 8 in 10 listings there, and a stated ambition to cover every corner of France. More deals are not ruled out.

cards.title: Differentiation through data and AI
cards.text: Meilleurs Agents valuations (a single property can be estimated 14–15 times a week), listing quality scores, natural-language search and owner tools aim to make SeLoger the agent's best lead source.

cards.title: A market that has only half recovered
cards.text: About 955k sales expected in 2026 against 1.2M in 2021; listings stay online ~110 days. Energy-rating reform in Jan 2027 and rate moves make buyers and sellers wait.

competitors.edge: Huge consumer reach; strongest in provinces and rural France
competitors.move: Push into Île-de-France; new packages and marketing aimed at SeLoger's urban core

competitors.model: Portal owned by agent networks and federations; professional listings only
competitors.edge: Agent loyalty; low entry pricing (e.g. €249/month for 100 listings, 2022); 3D maps
competitors.move: 220M visits in 2025 (+14%); national campaign; aims for the top spot

competitors.edge: Proven portal playbook in southern Europe
competitors.move: French launch in 2026 led by the former head of Leboncoin's real-estate unit
SeLoger has competed for private sellers since 2023
Lost court cases to SeLoger over scraping (Dec 2025, Jul 2026)

vulnerability.title: The agent trust problem
vulnerability.intro: SeLoger's paying customers are agents, and their trust is the business's main commercial vulnerability. This matters most for commercial, pricing, product and CEO roles.

timeline.text: Agent networks and federations launch Bien'ici to regain control of their data and listing prices.
SeLoger opens free private-seller listings and raises professional prices; some agents call for cutting access; the Guy Hoquet network president accuses SeLoger of turning on agents.
Bien'ici writes an open letter inviting agents to switch.
New France CEO reframes strategy around qualified leads and agent ROI; record new agency clients claimed in 2025.
FNAIM regional leaders publicly urge agents to pay only for listings they actually publish.

vulnerability.note: Company growth figures are self-reported. Current churn and agent satisfaction are not public.

conditions.title: A PE-backed pace
conditions.facts: KKR and CPP Investments have controlled AVIV since April 2025 (Axel Springer keeps 10%). AVIV is moving from a division of a media group to an independent, performance-driven company; Yad2 was sold in Dec 2025.
conditions.dayToDay: Expectations centre on growth, efficiency, execution and value creation. Pace often matters more than polish: decisions on good-enough information, short reporting cycles, and initiatives dropped quickly if they do not show measurable value.
conditions.helps: Bias to action, clear KPIs, visible results within months.
conditions.derails: Waiting for certainty or perfection; long unquantified programmes.

conditions.title: Local accountability, evolving decision rights
conditions.facts: France is gaining authority after the end of AVIV's pan-European platform project, but stays tied to the shared platform, Berlin group functions and group pricing councils.
conditions.dayToDay: Who owns what between Paris and Berlin is still being settled. Leaders often deliver before their mandate is fully defined, and must decide when to act locally and when to take an issue to the group.
conditions.helps: Creating clarity yourself, influence across the boundary.
conditions.derails: Acting as a local baron, or waiting for Berlin's permission.

conditions.title: A business in transformation with legacy complexity
conditions.facts: Nine French brands and verticals built partly through acquisitions (Logic-Immo, Meilleurs Agents, Ouest-France Immo), a shared group technology platform, and processes formed in a larger organisation.
conditions.dayToDay: Leaders must simplify structures, products, technology and ways of working while the business keeps selling to ~30,000 professional customers and integrating a new acquisition.
conditions.helps: Deciding what to merge, keep or retire; protecting revenue during change.
conditions.derails: Adding initiatives on top of complexity; simplifying so fast that customers are lost.

conditions.title: A lean organisation after the PSE
conditions.facts: 90 roles cut in 2024 and 275 (~30%) in 2026, about 80% of them engineers. Around 689 people remain in France.
conditions.dayToDay: Little slack anywhere. Every leader must stop work, prioritise hard and keep a smaller, tired team engaged; hiring is rarely the answer.
conditions.helps: Ruthless prioritisation, hands-on leadership, attention to morale.
conditions.derails: Same ambition with fewer people and no trade-offs.

conditions.title: A three-way cultural environment
conditions.facts: Paris teams shaped by French management culture; Berlin group functions; a group CEO who built his career at Avito in Russia, a COO from Adevinta, and North American investors.
conditions.dayToDay: Leaders translate continuously: fast, top-down signals from the group, explicit and consensus-first processes in Berlin, and a Paris organisation that expects hierarchy, debate and relationships.
conditions.helps: Reading context, adapting style, earning trust on all three sides.
conditions.derails: Over-adapting to the top and losing Paris, or resisting the group's pace.

conditions.title: The French social and management model
conditions.facts: The 2026 plan ran through a formal job-protection process with voluntary departures and majority union agreement; stated culture moved from conviviality to results orientation.
conditions.dayToDay: Change is negotiated with the works council and unions on legal timelines, which leaders must reconcile with the group's pace. Inside, authority is visible and ideas are debated hard.
conditions.helps: Credibility with employee representatives, well-argued positions.
conditions.derails: Announce-and-execute; treating consultation as a formality.

conditions.title: A contested market and repeated resets
conditions.facts: Three France leaders in five years, a strategy pendulum, a half-recovered market, and Leboncoin, Bien'ici and idealista pressing on SeLoger's core.
conditions.dayToDay: Teams watch whether a new direction will hold. Leaders must build credibility through consistency while reacting quickly to competitors.
conditions.helps: Steady direction, keeping promises, explaining the why.

environment.opportunity: Not simply to manage an established function, but to shape a more agile, effective and accountable organisation, delivering measurable business impact in a PE-backed environment.

skills.name: Delivering at PE pace while the organisation is still being redrawn
skills.definition: Gets measurable results within months even though AVIV's governance, France's decision rights, team structures and processes are still changing, and even though change in France runs through legal consultation with the works council.
skills.whyHere: KKR and CPP have owned AVIV since April 2025 with value-creation expectations; the group CEO is credited with growing Avito's revenue 30-fold; the 2026 PSE cut ~30% of France; France is re-localising after the European platform while integrating Ouest-France Immo; Paris–Berlin decision rights are not settled; group timelines are shorter than French consultation timelines.

markers.title: Pace over polish
markers.text: Decides with 70–80% of the information, ships, measures and adjusts. Knows the few things that must be perfect (legal steps, customer billing) and lets the rest be good enough.

markers.title: Creates their own map
markers.text: When reporting lines and ownership are unclear, writes down who decides what and by when, gets it agreed, and escalates only what truly needs the group.

markers.title: Numbers first
markers.text: Tracks a handful of metrics, reports in numbers on a monthly or quarterly rhythm, and says early when a number goes the wrong way.

evidence: Delivered a measurable result within 6–9 months of joining a business in restructuring or post-merger flux
Planned a transformation around consultation or other fixed constraints and still hit business milestones
Reported to a board or investors against value-creation targets
redFlags: Waits for a clean mandate, a full team or stable processes
Polishes past the point of value; long preparation, little delivery
Uses unclear governance or French process to explain missed results
skills.question: Tell me about a time you had to deliver a significant result while the organisation around you was being restructured and it was unclear who owned key decisions. What did you do in the first 30 days to create clarity, what did you deliver and by when, and what did you consciously leave imperfect?
skills.probe: What was the one thing you refused to compromise on, and why?
skills.confidenceNote: Highest-weighted capability for every senior role. The speed-over-polish expectation is search-partner input to confirm with the client.

skills.name: Using France's new autonomy without breaking the AVIV link
skills.definition: Takes the authority France is gaining on product, regional strategy and local services and uses it fully, while working through AVIV's shared platform, Berlin group functions and group pricing councils where France still depends on the group.
skills.whyHere: The 2026 re-localisation gave France its own CTO and product agenda, but pricing must align with the 'Group pricing architecture' in group councils, the listing platform is shared, owners set targets, and responsibilities between Paris and Berlin are still evolving.

markers.title: Argues hard, then commits
markers.text: Makes France's case to the group with data and pre-alignment; once the group decides, delivers it and keeps the team behind it.

markers.title: Owner, not messenger
markers.text: Presents group decisions to Paris as their own and takes local decisions without waiting for Berlin's permission.

markers.title: Does what they said
markers.text: Makes few promises to the group and keeps them; flags slippage before the deadline. This is how trust is earned with Berlin functions.

evidence: Led a unit or function while its decision rights with a parent were being renegotiated
Won a group decision for local needs
Delivered a local outcome on a shared group platform or service
Kept a team behind a group decision they had argued against
redFlags: Acts as an independent local baron and ignores group frameworks
Waits for headquarters' approval and relays its messages
Reopens decisions after they are made
skills.question: Tell me about a time your unit gained autonomy from a parent while still depending on its shared platforms or functions. Which decisions did you take locally, which did you take to the group, how did you decide, and what was the result?
skills.probe: Tell me about a group decision you argued against and then had to deliver. How did your team experience it?
skills.confidenceNote: All senior roles with group interfaces. Decision rights are inferred and need client validation.

skills.name: Simplifying a multi-brand legacy estate while it keeps selling
skills.definition: Reduces complexity across SeLoger's nine French brands and verticals, overlapping offers, processes and the shared AVIV technology, without disrupting revenue from ~30,000 professional customers or the spring selling season.
skills.whyHere: Brands accumulated through acquisitions (Logic-Immo 2018, Meilleurs Agents, Ouest-France Immo 2026); a European platform built and then de-prioritised; product capacity cut by ~30%; combined Ouest-France Immo offers planned within a year. Every function carries part of the legacy: finance systems, HR processes, tech stack, price plans.

markers.title: Stops before starting
markers.text: Retires or merges something before adding something new, and can say what they stopped.

markers.title: Respect for the customer's business
markers.text: Judges each simplification by its effect on agents, who are small businesses under pressure; protects customer-facing performance during migrations.

markers.title: Keeps what is worth keeping
markers.text: Decides explicitly what to merge, keep separate or leave alone, as with Ouest-France Immo's brand and local teams.

evidence: Rationalised products, brands, price plans or systems and showed the revenue effect
Simplified processes in their own function after a merger or restructuring
Integrated an acquisition while retaining its key customers and people
redFlags: Adds initiatives on top of old complexity
Simplifies so fast that customers or revenue are lost
Treats simplification as only an IT project
skills.question: Tell me about a time you simplified a portfolio of products, brands, systems or processes that had built up over years. How did you decide what to cut or merge, how did you protect revenue while doing it, and what was the measurable result?
skills.probe: What did you decide not to change, and why?

skills.name: Getting more from a post-PSE organisation that has seen three leaders and two strategies
skills.definition: Raises output and quality in a French organisation that cut 90 roles in 2024 and 275 in 2026, mostly engineers, and has had three France leaders and a strategy swing since 2021, by stopping low-value work, setting a steady direction and re-engaging people who watched colleagues leave.
skills.whyHere: Around 689 people in France are asked for more local features, more leads, more regions and an acquisition integration; career-opportunity ratings are weak; teams watch whether each new direction will hold.

markers.title: Sleeves rolled up
markers.text: Does whatever the work needs in a smaller team: writes the first draft, joins the customer call, looks at the data themselves.

markers.title: Steady in the churn
markers.text: Stays calm and consistent through change they do not control, absorbs uncertainty for the team, and explains what stays constant as well as what changes.

markers.title: Kind and candid
markers.text: Combines care for people who lived through cuts (SeLoger's stated value of bienveillance) with direct, honest messages about performance.

evidence: Led a team after major cuts and improved results within 12 months
Joined after several leadership changes and built credibility, starting with a listening phase
Kept key people through uncertainty, and can name how
redFlags: Same ambition with fewer people and no trade-offs
Arrives with a full new strategy and triggers another reset
Avoids hard people messages, or delivers them harshly
skills.question: Describe a time you led an organisation that had recently lost a significant share of its people and had seen several changes of direction. What did you change in the first 90 days, what did you deliberately leave alone, and how did you know people had re-engaged?
skills.probe: What did your team see from you in the week after the hardest announcement?
skills.confidenceNote: All senior roles; most acute in product, technology and operations, and for external hires.

skills.name: Leading French teams effectively
skills.definition: Leads, persuades and builds trust in the way French teams expect, using the working norms Erin Meyer's Culture Map describes for French business culture. This is a capability to assess in every candidate, French or not, never a question of nationality.
skills.whyHere: SeLoger's ~689 people, its customers, federations and unions work in French business culture. On Meyer's map France is principles-first, comfortable with open confrontation, hierarchical yet debate-driven in decisions, relationship-based in trust and high-context in communication.

markers.title: Reasoning before conclusions (Persuading)
markers.text: Builds the framework and the why before the recommendation; expects the logic to be tested.

markers.title: Debate as engagement (Disagreeing)
markers.text: Takes part in vigorous debate in the comité de direction, separates the idea from the person, and does not read challenge as resistance.

markers.title: Visible authority that can be challenged (Leading, Deciding)
markers.text: Holds the decision clearly as the leader, invites argument before deciding, and respects titles and channels.

markers.title: Relationships and reading between the lines (Trusting, Communicating)
markers.text: Invests time in people beyond tasks, and listens for what is implied rather than said.

evidence: Led teams in France or in a comparable principles-first, debate-driven culture and can describe how they adapted
Won support for a contested decision through argument rather than authority alone
Built working trust with employee representatives over time
redFlags: Opens with the conclusion and bullet points, and is judged superficial
Goes quiet or takes offence in open debate
Bypasses directors or ignores informal relationships
skills.question: Tell me about a time you had to win over a team that challenged your reasoning hard. How did you build your case, what happened in the debate, and what did you change in how you led them afterwards?
skills.probe: What did you learn about how that team built trust with a new leader?

skills.name: Bridging Paris, Berlin and a fast-moving group leadership
skills.definition: Translates between Paris teams, Berlin group functions that are explicit, consensus-first and schedule-driven, and a group leadership and investors who favour speed, directness and decisions from the top.
skills.whyHere: A group CEO with a decade at Avito in Russia and a COO from Adevinta, KKR and CPP as owners, German ownership since 2011 and a Berlin HQ. Reported further senior hires come from Russian business backgrounds (to validate).

markers.title: Two versions of every message
markers.text: Results-first for the group and investors, reasoning-first for Paris.

markers.title: Writes it down
markers.text: After every cross-border meeting, confirms decisions, owners and dates in writing, which Berlin needs and the group's high-context signals require.

markers.title: Takes blunt feedback well
markers.text: Receives direct criticism from the group without taking it personally, and passes it on to Paris with the reasoning, one to one where it is sensitive.

evidence: Worked between a head office and a local unit in different countries
Worked under a fast, top-down leadership and kept their own team engaged
Is described as credible by both a former boss and a former local team
redFlags: Over-adapts to the group top and loses Paris
Reads the group's directness as disrespect
Assumes one working style is right
skills.question: Tell me about a time you worked for a senior leader whose style was much faster and more top-down than your team was used to, while you also depended on a slower, process-driven function elsewhere. How did you adapt, what friction arose, and how did you resolve it?
skills.probe: How would the people on each side describe you?
skills.confidenceNote: All senior roles, most of all those with frequent group contact. Never a proxy for nationality, including similarity to the group leadership.
